slice: Same-executable timing controls with complete IN-table address traces

decision.finding: All 16 groups have matching complete address and hash sequences, but the first schedule stratum fails the predetermined timing interval width. Both strata use the same executable and fresh per-query planning-state clones.
decision.implication: Stabilizing the observed IN-table addresses is insufficient for these timing controls. The frozen result remains a failed control; no groups are excluded or replaced.
decision.counter_followup: Post-collection inspection retains all groups. Larger time differences accompany cycle and branch-miss differences, while instruction counts are nearly unchanged. This motivates locating the mispredicted branches; it does not establish their cause.

method.question: Does the existing same-executable timing control pass when retaining the fresh planning-state path in the last diagnostic build, and do observed table addresses remain stable?
method.implementation: No Rust changes or build. Reuse the exact planning-state executable, TaskContext reuse, fresh per-query SessionState clones, sorted resolver field release, native allocator settings and child-only fixed addresses. Both schedule labels refer to the same file and SHA256.
method.design: Reuse the existing 16-group, 64-process fully crossed control schedule and unchanged native seed indices 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14. Four temporal blocks, two groups per label per block. 32 warmups and 261 prepared plans per process. Equal launch paths and isolated gated phases.
method.analysis: For each of the two schedule strata, bootstrap whole four-process groups within the four temporal blocks, 10000 resamples, seed 88. Report the median group percentage change from process medians, process means, and instructions. Both timing intervals in both strata must fall entirely within +/-1% and include zero. Compare all 295 address/hash trace positions without filtering any runs.
method.correctness: Reference the prior 372 result/plan captures and 10 statement-state queries by binary and archive hashes; do not count them as new checks. Run the unchanged helper checks and eight new smoke processes for this driver setup, verifying selected-query results and traces.
method.stopping_rule: Exactly one fixed 16-group collection. Retain every attempt and failure. No conditional candidate comparison, no seed replacement, no outcome-based extension, no exclusion of unstable addresses. No builds, tests, source inspection or unrelated work during measurement. Freeze scripts and inputs before collection.
limits: This rebuilt diagnostic includes retained state, cold tracing and sorted field destruction; it is not the original release executable.
Stable occupied-element address bounds do not establish that all allocations or hardware state are identical.
Even passing self-controls would not establish an execution-time benefit, remove the original release interval, or adopt the optional type-inference patch.
Fresh-state and retained execution-context settings are fixed; this does not measure a state-reuse speedup.

counter_followup.scope: Post-collection descriptive analysis of all 16 groups. The frozen timing criteria and all runs remain unchanged.
counter_followup.caution: User cycles divided by task-clock is an aggregate proxy, not a direct APERF/MPERF clock measurement. Correlated cycle and branch-miss changes do not establish the source or cause of mispredictions.

reproduction.setup: Reuse the referenced byte-identical planning-state binary and frozen driver files in a fresh output directory. The native seed assignment and fully crossed schedule come unchanged from the earlier address-layout controls. Complete smoke checks before freezing and collecting. Reanalysis can use the retained collection groups and scripts without any executable rebuild. The post-collection counter analysis is descriptive and does not modify the original criteria.
